messages:
Zoe: FYI bringing reRankX v0.3-ptq4 (head+tail experimental) to staging. offline looked weird: NDCG slightly up but MRR drops concentrated on long-document queries. posting quick numbers + notes.

EvalBot: offline compare reRankX-v0.3-ptq4 -> baseline reRankX-v0.3-fp32
EvalBot: NDCG@10: 0.782 -> 0.789 (+0.007)
EvalBot: MRR@5: 0.622 -> 0.591 (-0.031)  <-- >80% of MRR loss from queries where the top candidates are long docs (>1024 tokens) and we apply different truncation heuristics

Harish: interesting. training/labeling used head+tail concatenation to preserve lead + trailing context. our eval harness default shows only the head snippet (first 512 tokens). that can reorder signals for long docs and change top1. is the PTQ path more sensitive to those context shifts? maybe.

Jenna: pasted two candidate renderings for one failing query (Qid: 44821):
Jenna: candidate A (train snippet head+tail): "Intro to async patterns... [snip mid] ...conclusion: use event loop optimizations."
Jenna: candidate B (eval head-only): "Intro to async patterns..."  (no tail context)
Jenna: in baseline A gets top1, in ptq build B ranks higher. truncation removed disambiguating tail sentence that mentions "event loop optimizations" which is a strong signal for relevance.

Zoe: that aligns with observed skew: NDCG (rank distribution) looks OK because later positions are stable, but MRR (top1 sensitivity) collapses when top candidate flips due to missing tail context.

Harish: triage steps i propose:
Harish: 1) regenerate the eval set with head+tail concatenation (mirrors train) and re-run the offline compare
Harish: 2) instrument eval CSV with fields: candidate_truncation_mode, candidate_order_seed, raw_candidate_bytes_hex
Harish: 3) run quant ablation: per-channel int8 & clip-outliers PTQ vs our current 4-bit PTQ to see kernel sensitivity to context length
Harish: command i will run for (1):
Harish: ```bash
Harish: python infra/eval_harness.py \
Harish:   --model reRankX-v0.3-ptq4 \
Harish:   --dataset longdoc_holdout \
Harish:   --truncation head_tail \
Harish:   --limit 15000 \
Harish:   --out /tmp/rerankx_headtail_eval.csv.gz
Harish: ```

EvalBot: quick re-eval with head+tail truncation applied:
EvalBot: NDCG@10: 0.782 -> 0.787 (+0.005)
EvalBot: MRR@5: 0.622 -> 0.614 (-0.008)
EvalBot: (MRR gap reduced significantly once tail context restored)

Jenna: good evidence that mismatch in candidate shaping caused a large chunk of the MRR regression. remaining delta might be kernel noise for long sequences where KV caching shapes attention math in PTQ. worth the ablation.

Harish: i'll run per-channel int8 and an alternate PTQ with outlier-clipping enabled tomorrow. if kernel ablation closes the remaining ~0.008 MRR we can pick the safer kernel for serving. if not, we should enforce head+tail truncation in serving to match train (small perf cost but preserves quality).

Zoe: tiny infra follow-up: can we add the truncation_mode & candidate_order_seed to the eval dashboard so future brings automatically note this? also add a sample_pairs artifact with raw bytes so QA can replay exact sequences.

DeployBot: canary deployment posted: reRankX v0.3-ptq4 -> canary (tag: canary-2026-05-02-rerankx)

Jenna: plan summary:
Jenna: - PR to eval_harness to add truncation_mode + raw_hex + order_seed to CSV (today)
Jenna: - Harish runs kernel ablations (tomorrow)
Jenna: - 50k head+tail vs head-only re-eval to estimate prod impact (Thu)
Jenna: - decision: prefer kernel change if cost-neutral; otherwise standardize truncation in serving.

Harish: uploading preliminary head+tail run to s3://redwood-evals/rerankx/v0.3/headtail_preview.csv.gz. will post diffs and tokenization mismatch stats when ablation finishes.

Zoe: thanks all. this felt subtle but glad we caught the shaping mismatch early. tagging @Jenna for the PR and @Harish for ablation outputs. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
